body: Hi, could you provide a stackblitz repro ? (I could not repoduce it with your code).

@JeanMeche indeed it seems to happen only when the service is injected in a standalone component.

Note: I don't use Angular myself anymore, so might good be that the way I injected the service in the standalone component is incorrect. If it's the root cause of the problem, then I would say it's just the error message that would deserve some love.

Here a sample repo:

```
git clone https://github.com/peterpeterparker/signals
cd signals
npm ci
npm run start
```

Thank you for your repro, I played with it a bit. 

* `standalone:true` is not an issue here
* `constructor` injection or `inject()` have the same effect
* The signals throws when the setter is called while a child  component is being instantiated 
* There is no issue if that same component is instantiated by the router. 
* This is no issue if the callback is called outside the `constructor`

issue.body:
This fix assures that templates functions executed in the creation mode are run outside of the reactive context. This avoids the situation where signal reads in a directive constructor (executed as part of the creation mode) would mark the host component as dirty.

Fixes #49871
